title: Atomic Upsert with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE & EXCLUDED Table
whatThisCodeCovers: Demonstrates an atomic, race-condition-free upsert pattern maintaining view counts and updating timestamps using the EXCLUDED pseudo-table and RETURNING clause.
code:
-- 1. Schema with unique constraint target
CREATE TABLE page_analytics (
    page_url TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    view_count BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    last_viewed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- 2. Atomic upsert: If url exists, increment count and update timestamp
INSERT INTO page_analytics (page_url, view_count, last_viewed_at)
VALUES ('/blog/postgresql-internals', 1, NOW())
ON CONFLICT (page_url) 
DO UPDATE SET
    view_count = page_analytics.view_count + EXCLUDED.view_count,
    last_viewed_at = EXCLUDED.last_viewed_at
RETURNING page_url, view_count, last_viewed_at;
breakdown: ON CONFLICT (page_url) targets the primary key unique index.
EXCLUDED.view_count references the proposed insert row value (1), adding it atomically to the existing row's view_count.
Eliminates application-level SELECT-then-INSERT race conditions under high concurrency.
RETURNING yields the newly updated row state in the same network roundtrip.
expectedOutput:
page_url                    | view_count | last_viewed_at
/blog/postgresql-internals  | 2          | 2026-11-04 11:20:00+00

title: Writable Common Table Expression (CTE) Data Archival Pipeline
whatThisCodeCovers: Combines a DELETE statement with an INSERT statement in a single atomic SQL transaction using a Writable CTE to archive expired session records.
code:
-- Move expired sessions to an archive table atomically in one query
WITH deleted_sessions AS (
    DELETE FROM user_sessions
    WHERE expires_at < NOW()
    RETURNING session_id, user_id, ip_address, created_at, NOW() AS archived_at
)
INSERT INTO session_archive (session_id, user_id, ip_address, created_at, archived_at)
SELECT session_id, user_id, ip_address, created_at, archived_at
FROM deleted_sessions
RETURNING session_id, user_id, archived_at;
breakdown: The CTE executes the DELETE operation and captures deleted rows via RETURNING.
The outer INSERT pipes the deleted rows directly into the session_archive table.
Guarantees that rows deleted from active storage are 100% saved in the archive; if anything fails, the entire transaction rolls back.
Eliminates multi-step application roundtrips.

title: Top-N Per Category Query using Indexed LATERAL Join
whatThisCodeCovers: Uses a CROSS JOIN LATERAL subquery backed by a composite B-Tree index to fetch the top 2 highest-value orders for every active customer with maximum efficiency.
code:
-- Composite index to make the lateral subquery an instant index seek
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_cust_amt ON orders (customer_id, amount DESC);

-- Fetch top 2 orders per active customer
SELECT 
    c.id AS customer_id, 
    c.company_name, 
    top_orders.id AS order_id, 
    top_orders.amount, 
    top_orders.created_at
FROM customers c
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT o.id, o.amount, o.created_at
    FROM orders o
    WHERE o.customer_id = c.id
    ORDER BY o.amount DESC
    LIMIT 2
) AS top_orders
WHERE c.is_active = true;
breakdown: LATERAL allows the subquery to reference c.id from the outer customers table.
Because the subquery has ORDER BY amount DESC LIMIT 2 matching idx_orders_cust_amt, Postgres only visits 2 index leaf entries per customer.
Vastly out-performs window functions (ROW_NUMBER) on large datasets because it never sorts or scans the full orders table.

title: Hierarchical Org-Chart Traversal with Depth & Breadcrumb Paths
whatThisCodeCovers: Traverses a multi-tier management reporting hierarchy using WITH RECURSIVE, calculating organization depth, reporting chains, and formatted breadcrumb trees.
code:
-- Recursive CTE to build employee management hierarchy
WITH RECURSIVE org_hierarchy AS (
    -- 1. Anchor: Top-level CEO (manager_id IS NULL)
    SELECT 
        employee_id, 
        name, 
        manager_id, 
        1 AS level, 
        name::TEXT AS management_chain,
        ARRAY[employee_id] AS hierarchy_path
    FROM employees
    WHERE manager_id IS NULL

    UNION ALL

    -- 2. Recursive Member: Direct reports of previous level
    SELECT 
        e.employee_id, 
        e.name, 
        e.manager_id, 
        o.level + 1, 
        o.management_chain || ' -> ' || e.name,
        o.hierarchy_path || e.employee_id
    FROM employees e
    JOIN org_hierarchy o ON e.manager_id = o.employee_id
)
SELECT level, name, management_chain
FROM org_hierarchy
ORDER BY hierarchy_path;
breakdown: Anchor query initializes the working table with root executives where manager_id IS NULL.
Recursive query joins employees against org_hierarchy using manager_id = employee_id.
ARRAY[employee_id] provides hierarchical sorting so direct reports appear directly beneath their manager.
Terminates automatically when no employees report to the lowest level.
expectedOutput:
level | name       | management_chain
1     | Sarah CEO  | Sarah CEO
2     | Bob VP Eng | Sarah CEO -> Bob VP Eng
3     | Carol Dev  | Sarah CEO -> Bob VP Eng -> Carol Dev

title: Cycle-Protected Directed Graph Path Traversal
whatThisCodeCovers: Navigates complex directed cyclic graphs (e.g. social networks, supply chain dependencies) using array visited-checks and PostgreSQL 14+ CYCLE clause.
code:
-- Find all transitive dependencies while stopping cycles
WITH RECURSIVE component_deps AS (
    -- Anchor: root component
    SELECT 
        assembly_id, 
        part_id, 
        1 AS depth, 
        ARRAY[assembly_id] AS visited_ids,
        false AS is_cycle
    FROM bill_of_materials
    WHERE assembly_id = 'ENGINE-01'

    UNION ALL

    -- Recursive: sub-components
    SELECT 
        b.assembly_id, 
        b.part_id, 
        cd.depth + 1, 
        cd.visited_ids || b.assembly_id,
        b.part_id = ANY(cd.visited_ids)
    FROM bill_of_materials b
    JOIN component_deps cd ON b.assembly_id = cd.part_id
    WHERE NOT (b.assembly_id = ANY(cd.visited_ids)) -- Stop infinite cycles!
)
SELECT depth, assembly_id, part_id, is_cycle FROM component_deps;
breakdown: Maintains visited_ids array across recursive iterations.
The WHERE condition NOT (b.assembly_id = ANY(cd.visited_ids)) halts recursive traversal before entering an infinite loop.
Safeguards against corrupted data structures or circular dependencies in manufacturing BOMs.
expectedOutput:
depth | assembly_id | part_id    | is_cycle
1     | ENGINE-01   | PISTON-01  | f
2     | PISTON-01   | RING-02    | f

title: Time-Series Moving Average with ROWS vs RANGE Framing
whatThisCodeCovers: Calculates physical 3-row moving averages and time-interval 7-day rolling revenue using window function frames (ROWS vs RANGE).
code:
-- Compare physical row window vs time-based interval window
SELECT 
    sold_at, 
    daily_revenue,
    -- 1. Physical 3-day moving average (strictly 3 preceding rows)
    AVG(daily_revenue) OVER (
        ORDER BY sold_at 
        ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS physical_3_day_avg,
    -- 2. Time-based 7-day rolling sum (handles gaps/missing days gracefully)
    SUM(daily_revenue) OVER (
        ORDER BY sold_at 
        RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '7 days' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS rolling_7_day_revenue
FROM revenue_history
ORDER BY sold_at DESC;
breakdown: ROWS counts physical tuple offsets; if days are skipped, it still takes 3 rows.
RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL evaluates timestamp values directly; if weekends are skipped, it sums only the actual past 7 calendar days.
Provides robust statistical calculations for financial analytics.

title: Table Synchronization with PostgreSQL 15+ MERGE Statement
whatThisCodeCovers: Synchronizes a primary customer table with an external incoming staging batch using MERGE to handle matched updates, conditional deletions, and new insertions.
code:
-- Synchronize accounts table from external incoming feed
MERGE INTO customer_accounts target
USING staging_account_updates source
ON target.account_id = source.account_id
-- 1. If closed in source, delete from target
WHEN MATCHED AND source.status = 'CLOSED' THEN
    DELETE
-- 2. If balance changed, update
WHEN MATCHED THEN
    UPDATE SET 
        balance = source.balance, 
        updated_at = NOW()
-- 3. If new account, insert
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN
    INSERT (account_id, balance, status, created_at)
    VALUES (source.account_id, source.balance, source.status, NOW());
breakdown: MERGE joins target with source on account_id.
Handles updates, deletes, and inserts conditionally in one atomic statement.
Standard ANSI SQL syntax added in PostgreSQL 15 for batch ETL pipelines.

title: JSON Schema Validation using Native CHECK Constraints
whatThisCodeCovers: Enforces structural typing, mandatory keys, and value bounds on JSONB columns without installing third-party extensions.
code:
-- Enforce strict JSONB schema on write
CREATE TABLE service_configs (
    service_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    config JSONB NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT check_valid_config CHECK (
        -- 1. Must be a JSON object
        jsonb_typeof(config) = 'object' AND
        -- 2. Must contain required keys
        config ?& ARRAY['port', 'workers', 'env'] AND
        -- 3. Port must be a number between 1024 and 65535
        jsonb_typeof(config->'port') = 'number' AND
        (config->>'port')::INT BETWEEN 1024 AND 65535 AND
        -- 4. Environment must match enum values
        config->>'env' IN ('development', 'staging', 'production')
    )
);
breakdown: Enforces data integrity before rows hit disk storage.
Guarantees that bad API payloads fail immediately with constraint violation errors.
Combines schema flexibility for optional keys with relational rigor for core attributes.

title: Continuous Interval Operations with Timestamp Range Types
whatThisCodeCovers: Models temporal promotion windows using tstzrange, testing element containment (@>), interval intersection (*), and adjacency (-|-).

-- Promotions with continuous date boundaries
CREATE TABLE promotional_discounts (
    promo_code TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    valid_window TSTZRANGE NOT NULL,
    discount_pct NUMERIC(4, 2) NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO promotional_discounts VALUES 
('SUMMER26', tstzrange('2026-06-01 00:00:00+00', '2026-09-01 00:00:00+00', '[)'), 20.00);

-- 1. Check if promo is valid right now (@> operator)
SELECT promo_code, discount_pct 
FROM promotional_discounts 
WHERE valid_window @> '2026-07-15 12:00:00+00'::TIMESTAMPTZ;

FROM promotional_discounts;

title: Composite Types (CREATE TYPE AS) in PL/pgSQL Function Signatures
whatThisCodeCovers: Declares a custom Composite Type to return structured multi-attribute output from stored procedures and PL/pgSQL functions.
code:
-- Define structured composite return type
CREATE TYPE inventory_reorder_summary AS (
    supplier_name TEXT,
    item_count INT,
    estimated_cost NUMERIC(12, 2)
);

-- Stored function returning the composite type
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION generate_reorder_quote(target_warehouse_id INT)
RETURNS inventory_reorder_summary
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    result inventory_reorder_summary;
BEGIN
    SELECT 
        s.name, 
        COUNT(i.id), 
        SUM(i.unit_cost * i.reorder_qty)
    INTO result
    FROM inventory i
    JOIN suppliers s ON s.id = i.supplier_id
    WHERE i.warehouse_id = target_warehouse_id AND i.stock_qty < i.reorder_threshold
    GROUP BY s.name
    LIMIT 1;

    RETURN result;
END;
$$;

-- Query the composite result
SELECT (generate_reorder_quote(1)).supplier_name, (generate_reorder_quote(1)).estimated_cost;
breakdown: CREATE TYPE AS defines named field structures.
Functions return strongly typed record objects rather than generic untyped tuples.
Fields are accessed using (composite_col).field notation.
expectedOutput:
supplier_name       | estimated_cost
Industrial Supplies | 14500.00

title: Array Unnesting with Positional Tracking (WITH ORDINALITY)

FROM project_tasks t,

-- Configure postgresql.conf to capture lock waits and deadlocks

-- SESSION A:
BEGIN;
UPDATE inventory SET stock = stock - 1 WHERE item_id = 1; -- locks 1

-- SESSION B:
BEGIN;
UPDATE inventory SET stock = stock - 1 WHERE item_id = 2; -- locks 2

-- SESSION A:
UPDATE inventory SET stock = stock - 1 WHERE item_id = 2; -- WAITING for Session B!

-- SESSION B:
UPDATE inventory SET stock = stock - 1 WHERE item_id = 1; 
-- DEADLOCK DETECTED!
-- ERROR: deadlock detected (SQLSTATE 40P01)
-- Detail: Process 101 waits for ShareLock on transaction 102; Process 102 waits for ShareLock on transaction 101.

title: Synchronous Audit Logging Trigger with pg_trigger_depth() Protection
whatThisCodeCovers: Captures full row mutation audit logs inside an ACID trigger, utilizing pg_trigger_depth() to prevent infinite trigger recursion loops.
conceptsCovered: AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE
code:
-- Audit log schema
CREATE TABLE audit_log_entries (
    log_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    table_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    action TEXT NOT NULL,
    user_id TEXT,
    old_row JSONB,
    new_row JSONB,
    occurred_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Trigger function
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION track_audit_history() 
RETURNS TRIGGER LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    -- Prevent infinite trigger recursion loops if audit table triggers another trigger
    IF pg_trigger_depth() > 1 THEN
        RETURN NEW;
    END IF;

    INSERT INTO audit_log_entries (
        table_name, 
        action, 
        user_id, 
        old_row, 
        new_row
    ) VALUES (
        TG_TABLE_NAME,
        TG_OP,
        NULLIF(current_setting('app.current_user_id', true), ''),
        CASE WHEN TG_OP IN ('UPDATE', 'DELETE') THEN to_jsonb(OLD) ELSE NULL END,
        CASE WHEN TG_OP IN ('INSERT', 'UPDATE') THEN to_jsonb(NEW) ELSE NULL END
    );

    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

-- Attach trigger
CREATE TRIGGER audit_accounts_trigger
AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON user_accounts
FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION track_audit_history();
breakdown: Captures synchronous audit records in the same transaction as the modifying operation.
pg_trigger_depth() > 1 terminates cascading recursion safely.
to_jsonb(OLD) and to_jsonb(NEW) serialize row states automatically.
expectedOutput:
CREATE FUNCTION
CREATE TRIGGER
